item.title: A dog found in Connecticut had bullet fragments lodged in her face; $6,000 reward for information
item.description: Gracie, a female pitbull mix, was discovered in Connecticut with bullet fragments embedded in her face. After a challenging rescue operation lasting several days, she is now safe. Vets confirmed she was shot with a high-velocity pistol, inflicting severe injuries. The local community is rallying to cover her medical costs while authorities search for the shooter, offering a $6,000 reward for any leads that result in an arrest.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Guide dog Eddie has won the 16th annual American Humane Hero Dog Award
item.description: Luis Rodriguez, a legally blind individual, has found significant support from his guide dog, Eddie. This three-year-old Labrador retriever has transformed Rodriguez's daily experiences, providing him with the confidence to take spontaneous adventures that once felt out of reach. With specialized training to navigate obstacles safely, Eddie has not only become a vital companion but is now also featured online, raising awareness about living with visual impairment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Louisiana lumber firms lose appeal over alleged damage from widening gas pipeline canals
item.description: Two Louisiana lumber companies have lost their legal battle against a gas company over canals they said had widened and damaged their land. The appeals court upheld the dismissal of their 2018 lawsuit, ruling that the companies had waited too long to take legal action. One judge disagreed, saying the case should have been examined further.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meg Ryan's renovated Montecito estate sells for $18 million after two resales in 2025 and 2026
item.description: Meg Ryan's former estate in Montecito has seen significant changes throughout its brief ownership history. After acquiring the property for $9.5 million in 2021, Ryan renovated and sold it for an impressive $16.8 million in 2025. The subsequent owner tried to list it at elevated prices but faced challenges, ultimately achieving a sale of $18 million after a price drop just four months later.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Canadian ranch's 55,000 acres earn first verified grassland carbon credits under national protocol
item.description: More than 55,000 acres of native prairie in Alberta have received carbon credit verification for conservation efforts. This property is one of the largest untouched grasslands in North America, and it retains vital carbon stored in the soil. The verification is the result of two decades of discussions involving landowners and conservation organizations. The project generates carbon offset credits by preventing land conversion into cropland.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Odyssey cruise ship that left 200 passengers stranded, impounded in Singapore
item.description: The cruise ship named Odyssey has been detained in Singapore due to financial complications faced by its operating company. Authorities reported that the vessel arrived empty from Cambodia after around 200 passengers were asked to disembark when operations ceased unexpectedly. Rising fuel costs were identified as the primary factor behind this financial distress, prompting concerns among investors regarding the viability of the cruise experience.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Lashkar terrorist Hafiz Saeed's political outfit loses Pakistan's parliamentary bypoll
item.description: A parliamentary by-election in NA-77 constituency resulted in a defeat for the Pakistan Markazi Muslim League. The ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz retained the seat with Rashid Bashir Virk receiving over 43,000 votes. Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar, from the PMML, received more than 30,000 votes but lost in the election. The turnout was low and allegations of electoral malpractice were reported, including one village boycotting the vote.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Rend Lake Habitat Project: Crews sink 875 Christmas trees for fish; holiday waste aids ecosystem
item.description: In a remarkable conservation effort in southern Illinois, 875 discarded Christmas trees have been transformed into valuable underwater habitats for fish. This collaborative initiative, involving local businesses, fisheries biologists, and dedicated volunteers, aims to bolster aquatic life in Rend Lake. The trees offer shelter to juvenile fish and play a crucial role in the ecosystem's food chain.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas appeals court denies bank recovery on $29m Ponzi-linked loan guarantee
item.description: In a significant legal decision, a Texas appeals court has affirmed a lower court's ruling regarding PlainsCapital Bank's unsuccessful attempt to recoup funds related to a $29 million loan guarantee associated with a Ponzi scheme. Despite the bank conceding contract defenses, the evidence presented was deemed inadequate for the guaranteed sum, highlighting the bank's inability to substantiate recoverable damages and crucial proof.

item.title: 39 dead as migrant boat capsizes off Senegal on perilous route to Canary Islands
item.description: At least 39 migrants died when a boat capsized off the coast of Senegal while heading to Spain. The small vessel was en route to the Canary Islands when it overturned, prompting ongoing search operations. Officials confirmed that all recovered bodies were Senegalese nationals, with many still missing. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye expressed condolences and urged citizens to avoid dangerous crossings.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Finland is building a 100-million-gallon water pit to store 18,000 MWh of heat, enough to supply 20,000 people
item.description: Hyvinkaa is embarking on an ambitious project to fill an old gravel pit with 100 million gallons of water, designed for thermal energy storage. This facility is set to provide approximately 25% of the city's heating requirements during the colder months. While construction is scheduled to continue until late April 2027, the facility is expected to start charging by late summer 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How ancient Peruvians responded to climate disasters
item.description: Researchers examined over 1,500 ancient Peruvian skeletons to understand societal responses to climate disasters. Findings reveal that violence was rare even during El Niño flooding events that severely impacted food availability. Interestingly, mass human sacrifices were observed without corresponding everyday violence among the population. This suggests that ancient societies may have adapted creatively to ecological crises. Overall, the study highlights the choices societies make in response to environmental challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
